purpose: Decide whether the served lettuce model can be validated against a source it was not trained on. Each candidate is recorded with what it actually publishes, what the model would need, and a verdict. Nothing here is used to fit or tune anything.

requirement.note: A candidate must report all four inputs per observation, not study averages, or the comparison would mix one PPFD with a yield averaged over several PPFDs.

trainingSource.title: Plant Factories Are Heating Up: lettuce growth dataset
trainingSource.reason: This is the dataset the model was trained on (1,648 observations over 4 experiments). It cannot also be the external validation.

candidates.title: Vertical farming for lettuce production in limited space: a case study in Northern Thailand
candidates.authors: Wicharuck, Khongdee, Man, Syahputra, Yalangkan, Chaiphak, Chaichana
candidates.dataAvailability: Raw data supplied as Supplemental File (supp-1).
candidates.reason: In domain on every input and reports fresh weight per plant at a stated day after transplanting. The published figures are study averages across three light levels, so using them against a single PPFD would be a mismatched comparison. The per-level raw table has to be transcribed from the supplemental file first, verbatim, before any prediction is made.
candidates.blocking: Per-level raw table not yet transcribed; no value has been entered here to avoid inventing one.

candidates.title: Vertical farming increases lettuce yield per unit area compared to conventional horizontal hydroponics
candidates.reason: Air temperature 16-18 C sits below the model's declared 20-32 C applicability domain, and a mother-and-daughter per-day observation series with root-zone temperature is not published in the accessible text. The model must decline this source rather than extrapolate into it.
candidates.blocking: Below the declared domain; harvest day and root-zone temperature also not reported in the accessible text.

candidates.title: Comparative Study of Lettuce and Radish Grown Under Red and Blue LEDs and White Fluorescent Lamps

reported.note: Equal-PPF comparison of red+blue LED against white fluorescent for lettuce and radish, with n and SD printed on the poster's Table 1.

candidates.reason: The measurement table is an image on a one-page poster, not machine-readable text, and the design varies light spectrum at fixed PPFD. The served lettuce model has no spectrum input, so even a perfect transcription would test an input the model does not accept.
candidates.blocking: No spectrum input in the model; table not machine-readable.

conclusion.statement: No independent source currently validates the lettuce model. The strongest available candidate is PeerJ 17085, which is in domain on every input and only waits on a verbatim transcription of its per-level table; that transcription is the next concrete step and is deliberately not being replaced by a study average.
conclusion.whatThisDoesNotMean: It does not mean the model is wrong, and it does not mean the leave-one-experiment-out cross-validation is external. Four experiments from one research group remain one source.
